title: "LEARNING PATHWAYS"

![](/images/uq1.jpg){ width=100% }

Welcome to LADAL learning pathways. This page is for independent learners who want to get started with LADAL content, but want a bit more structure than our stand-alone tutorials. Here, we have grouped together related tutorials into short, self-directed courses on key topics LADAL users may be interested in.
 
# Introduction to Corpus Linguistics


This pathway provides an introduction to key methods in corpus linguistics using R.

**[Introduction to Text Analysis](/tutorials/introta/introta.html)**   

This tutorial introduces Text Analysis, i.e. computer-based analysis of language data or the (semi-)automated extraction of information from text.

**[Getting Started with R](/tutorials/intror/intror.html)**

This tutorial shows how to get started with R and it specifically focuses on R for analysing language data but it offers valuable information for anyone who wants to get started with R. For the purposes of this learning pathway, focus on the first four sections (up to Working with Tables).

**[Handling tables in R](/tutorials/table/table.html)**

This tutorial shows how to work with tables and how to tabulate data in R.

**[Concordancing (keywords-in-context)](/tutorials/kwics/kwics.html)**

This tutorial introduces how to find words or phrases in text and display concordances, a so-called keyword-in-context (KWIC) display, with R.

**[Collocation and N-gram Analysis](/tutorials/coll/coll.html)**

This tutorial introduces collocation analysis and identifying N-grams with R and shows how to extract and visualise semantic links between words. 

**[Keyness and Keyword Analysis](/tutorials/key/key.html)**

This tutorial introduces keyness analysis and identifying keywords with R and shows how to visualise keywords.

**[Corpus Linguistics with R](/tutorials/corplingr/corplingr.html)**

This section presents different case studies or use cases that highlight how to do corpus-based analyses by implementing procedures shown in other LADAL tutorials.

# Introduction to Text Analysis


This pathway provides an introduction to key methods in text analysis using R.

**[Introduction to Text Analysis](/tutorials/introta/introta.html)**

This tutorial introduces Text Analysis, i.e. computer-based analysis of language data or the (semi-)automated extraction of information from text.

**[Reproducible Research](/tutorials/repro/repro.html)**

This tutorial introduces options to make your research and workflows efficient and reproducible.

**[Getting Started with R](/tutorials/intror/intror.html)**

This tutorial shows how to get started with R and it specifically focuses on R for analysing language data but it offers valuable information for anyone who wants to get started with R. For the purposes of this learning pathway, focus on the first four sections (up to Working with Tables).

**[Reproducible Research](/tutorials/repro/repro.html)**

This tutorial introduces options to make your research and workflows efficient and reproducible.

**[Practical Overview of Selected Text Analytics Methods](/tutorials/textanalysis/textanalysis.html)**

This tutorial showcases some basic but useful methods for text analysis and serves as a practical overview or introduction to Text analytics and distant reading.

**[String Processing](/tutorials/string/string.html)**

This tutorial introduces string processing and this can be used when working with language data.

**[Topic Modeling](/tutorials/topic/topic.html)** 
 
This tutorial introduces topic modelling using R.

**[Sentiment Analysis](/tutorials/sentiment/sentiment.html)**

This tutorial introduces sentiment analysis and shows how to perform it in R.

**[Network Analysis](/tutorials/net/net.html)**

This tutorial introduces network analysis using R. Network analysis is a method for visualisation that can be used to represent various types of data.

# Introduction to Statistics in the Humanities and Social Sciences


This pathway provides a simple introduction to statistics and quantitative research. It is aimed at learners with a background in the humanities and social sciences who have little to no prior knowledge in statistics.

**[Introduction to Quantitative Reasoning](/tutorials/introquant/introquant.html)**

This tutorial takes a philosophical or history-of-ideas approach and introduces the logical and cognitive underpinnings of the scientific method. 

**[Basic Concepts in Quantitative Research](/tutorials/basicquant/basicquant.html)**

This tutorial introduces basic concepts of data analysis and quantitative research.

**[Getting started](/tutorials/intror/intror.html)**

This tutorial shows how to get started with R and it specifically focuses on R for analysing language data but it offers valuable information for anyone who wants to get started with R. 

**[Handling tables in R](/tutorials/table/table.html)**

This tutorial shows how to work with tables and how to tabulate data in R.

**[Descriptive Statistics](/tutorials/dstats/dstats.html)**

This tutorial focuses on how to describe and summarise data in R.

**[Introduction to Data Viz](/tutorials/introviz/introviz.html)**

This tutorial introduces data visualisation using R and shows how to modify different types of visualisations in the ggplot framework in R.

**[Basic Inferential Statistics](/tutorials/basicstatz/basicstatz.html)**
 
This tutorial introduces basic inferential procedures for null-hypothesis hypothesis testing.
